newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Firm announces deal on massive Indonesia gold find.
newsitem.headline: Firm announces deal on massive Indonesia gold find.

text.p: Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Monday the company and its Indonesian partners had formed a joint venture with U.S. firm Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop Indonesia's huge Busang gold find.

It said in a statement faxed to Reuters: "The joint venture will be 45 percent owned by Bre-X, 30 percent by two Indonesian companies and their partners, 10 percent by the Republic of Indonesia and 15 percent by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold."
Bre-X also announced in a separate statement that it had increased its estimate of gold reserves at Busang by 13.6 million ounces to 70.95 million ounces.
It also said the average overall grade had increased.
"This is a great day for both Bre-X shareholders and for the people of Indonesia," Bre-X chief executive officer David Walsh said in the statement announcing the deal.
Industry sources said that Bre-X, Freeport and Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan on behalf of Indonesian interests had signed a memorandum of understanding on Sunday covering the agreement.
There was no mention of Canadian mining firm Barrick Gold Corp which had earlier been lined up by the Indonesian government as the potential partner for Bre-X in developing Busang.
The government had given the two companies until Monday to settle with their local partners before getting the go-ahead to develop Busang.

The Bre-X statement said Freeport would provide approximately $400 million, or 25 percent of the estimated cost of constructing the mining complex in the remote rainforests of Indonesia's East Kalimantan province on Borneo island.
Freeport, which runs one of the world's biggest copper and gold mines in Indonesia's Irian Jaya province through PT Freeport Indonesia, would be the sole operator of the Busang mine, Bre-X said.
"Freeport will also provide up to $1.2 billion in additional funding for the venture through a commitment from a major financial institution.
"The financial strength will allow for the joint venture to proceed without any further dilution to shareholders," it said.
Industry sources said New York's Chase Manhattan Corp would provide the loan, which it was expected to syndicate.
